# ferentin_data_protection_policy (Resource)

Tenant data-protection (DLP / "Data & Content Protection") policy. Selects sensitive-data and security detectors (via profiles and/or individual detectors), assigns a per-detector or default effect (`tokenize` / `redact` / `block` / `log`), and scopes enforcement to LLM and/or MCP input/output. Optional `criteria` apply the policy conditionally (ABAC).

## Import

```
terraform import ferentin_data_protection_policy.example <tenant_id>/<policy_id>
```

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ferentin_data_protection_policy" "prod" {
  name        = "prod-pii-and-exfil"
  description = "Tokenize US PII; log exfiltration URLs on responses"
  priority    = 100

  # Three-layer detector selection.
  enabled_profiles   = ["US_PII", "EXFILTRATION_DEFENSE"]
  enabled_detectors  = { "DATABASE_URL" = true }
  disabled_detectors = { "EU_VAT" = true }

  # Per-detector effect overrides + the default for everything else.
  effects = {
    "US_SSN"           = "tokenize"
    "EXFILTRATION_URL" = "log"
  }
  default_effect = "redact"

  # Per-detector tuning.
  detector_thresholds = { "US_SSN" = 0.95 }
  detector_configs = {
    "EXFILTRATION_URL" = jsonencode({
      minConfidenceScore = 0.5
      hostSuffixDenylist = ["webhook.site"]
    })
  }

  # Format-preserving encryption (required when any effect is "tokenize").
  fpe_key_id  = "dlp-fpe-2026"
  tweak_scope = "conversation"

  # Where the policy runs.
  apply_to_llm_input  = true
  apply_to_llm_output = true
  apply_to_mcp_output = true

  # Optional ABAC: apply only to the legal department.
  criteria = [
    {
      operator = "AND"
      type     = "claims"
      conditions = [
        {
          field    = "department"
          operator = "equals"
          value    = jsonencode("legal")
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

# Endpoint data protection: evaluated on enrolled devices against AI coding
# agents' tool calls, prompts and tool output. Separate from the cloud scopes
# above — a policy can carry both, but opting in is explicit per scope.
resource "ferentin_data_protection_policy" "endpoint_secrets" {
  name             = "endpoint-secrets"
  enabled_profiles = ["SECRETS"]
  default_effect   = "block"
  blocked_message  = "Blocked: this looks like a credential. Ask #security if it is not."

  apply_to_llm_input  = false
  apply_to_llm_output = false

  apply_to_tool_input   = true # shell commands, fetched URLs and bodies, file writes
  apply_to_prompt_input = true # what a developer submits to the agent
  apply_to_tool_output  = true # what a tool returns, before the model sees it

  # Withhold tool output the device could not scan (best effort).
  tool_output_unscanned_action = "withhold"

  # Deny an MCP tool call whose arguments were too large to scan whole
  # (Claude Code and Cursor only).
  tool_input_unscanned_action = "block"

  # Empty or unset = every enrolled device. Reference
  # ferentin_device_group.<name>.group_id to narrow it.
  device_group_ids = []
}

# A2A data protection: scans what is sent to A2A agents and what they return.
# An A2A skill served as an MCP tool is scanned once, under these scopes.
resource "ferentin_data_protection_policy" "a2a_pii" {
  name             = "a2a-pii"
  enabled_profiles = ["US_PII", "SECRETS"]
  default_effect   = "redact"

  apply_to_llm_input  = false
  apply_to_llm_output = false

  apply_to_a2a_input  = true # messages, data, files and metadata sent to agents
  apply_to_a2a_output = true # agent replies, task status messages and artifacts

  # A file that cannot be scanned (binary, too large, or a file link) is refused.
  a2a_unscannable_file_action = "block"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)

### Optional

- `a2a_unscannable_file_action` (String) With an A2A scope: what happens to a file that cannot be scanned (an inline file that is not text or is too large, and every file link). `block` refuses it; `pass_and_count` lets it through and records it. Omit to keep the current value (`block` on a new policy).
- `apply_to_a2a_input` (Boolean) Scan everything sent to A2A agents: message text, data, files, and the metadata on parts, messages and artifacts. An A2A skill served as an MCP tool is scanned once, under the A2A scopes; the MCP scopes do not apply to it. Omit to keep the current value (`false` on a new policy); removing it from config does not turn it off.
- `apply_to_a2a_output` (Boolean) Scan A2A agent replies, task status messages and artifacts. Omit to keep the current value (`false` on a new policy); removing it from config does not turn it off.
- `apply_to_llm_input` (Boolean) Scan LLM user input/prompts. Default `true`.
- `apply_to_llm_output` (Boolean) Scan LLM responses. Default `true`.
- `apply_to_mcp_input` (Boolean) Scan MCP tool-call arguments. Default `false`.
- `apply_to_mcp_output` (Boolean) Scan MCP tool-call results. Default `false`.
- `apply_to_prompt_input` (Boolean) Evaluate on enrolled endpoints, against prompts developers submit to AI agents, before they reach the model. A prompt cannot be rewritten, so `redact` and `tokenize` are enforced as `block`. Default `false`.
- `apply_to_tool_input` (Boolean) Evaluate on enrolled endpoints, against AI agents' native tool calls: shell commands, fetched URLs and bodies, file writes. `tokenize` is enforced there as `redact` (as `block` on an agent that cannot rewrite tool input). Default `false`.
- `apply_to_tool_output` (Boolean) Evaluate on enrolled endpoints, against what a tool returns before the agent's model sees it: `block` replaces the affected text with a notice and `redact` masks the match. The tool has already run, so this protects the model's context, not the action. Enforced only on agents whose hooks can replace tool output. Default `false`.
- `blocked_message` (String) User-facing message returned when a request is blocked.
- `criteria` (Attributes List) ABAC criteria for conditional application. Each entry combines `conditions` with a logical operator (`AND`/`OR`); multiple criteria entries are themselves ANDed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--criteria))
- `default_effect` (String) Effect applied when a matched detector has no per-detector override. One of `tokenize` / `redact` / `block` / `log`. Defaults to `redact`.
- `description` (String)
- `detector_configs` (Map of String) Per-detector validator-config overrides, shallow-merged over the catalog default at scan time. Keyed by detector ID; each value is a JSON object produced with `jsonencode(...)`, e.g. `{ "EXFILTRATION_URL" = jsonencode({ minConfidenceScore = 0.5 }) }`.
- `detector_thresholds` (Map of Number) Per-detector confidence threshold override (0.0–1.0), keyed by detector ID.
- `device_group_ids` (Set of String) Device groups this policy targets on its endpoint scopes — reference `ferentin_device_group.<name>.group_id`. Empty or unset = **every device in the tenant**. Ignored by edge and cloud enforcement. At most 100.

~> A group id belonging to another tenant is rejected with 404 (the platform deliberately does not distinguish "not yours" from "does not exist").
- `disabled_detectors` (Map of Boolean) Detectors to exclude even though a profile pulls them in, keyed by detector ID (e.g. `{ "EU_VAT" = true }`).
- `effects` (Map of String) Per-detector effect override, keyed by detector ID. One of `tokenize` / `redact` / `block` / `log`. Each key must be a detector this policy enables (`enabled_profiles` plus `enabled_detectors`, minus `disabled_detectors`); an effect applies only to detectors its own policy enables. The API refuses any other key, including one the catalog does not know, with a `400` naming it. An update that changes `effects`, `enabled_profiles`, `enabled_detectors` or `disabled_detectors` is judged on the result, so dropping a profile while keeping an effect on one of its detectors is refused too: remove the effect, or enable the detector in this policy.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the policy is enforced. Default `true`.
- `enabled_detectors` (Map of Boolean) Individual detectors to enable beyond the selected profiles, keyed by detector ID (e.g. `{ "DATABASE_URL" = true }`).
- `enabled_profiles` (List of String) Detector profiles to enable, e.g. `US_PII`, `EU_PII`, `SECRETS`, `EXFILTRATION_DEFENSE`. Profile names are catalog data (see the `ferentin_data_protection_profiles` data source) and validated server-side. A profile grows with the catalog: a detector the platform adds to it runs in every policy that selects the profile, under `default_effect`, with no change in the plan. To keep one out, add it to `disabled_detectors`; to give it another effect, name it in `effects`.
- `fpe_key_id` (String) Key identifier for format-preserving encryption. Required by the platform when any effect is `tokenize`.
- `priority` (Number) Evaluation priority (1 = highest). Defaults to 100.
- `tenant_id` (String)
- `tool_input_unscanned_action` (String) With `apply_to_tool_input`: what a device does with an MCP tool call whose arguments it could not scan whole (cut to fit its hook frame, or past the agent's 1 MiB payload limit from agent 1.2.74). `allow` runs the call and records it as too large; `block` denies it with its own message, never reported as a detection. Omit to keep the current value (`allow` on a new policy).

~> Acts only on Claude Code and Cursor; Codex, Copilot and Antigravity accept it and do nothing. It covers MCP call arguments only (not shell commands, file writes or fetches), and only while the policy has a tool-input detector that blocks or redacts.
- `tool_output_unscanned_action` (String) With `apply_to_tool_output`: what a device does with tool output it knows it could not scan (over its size cap, or out of scan time). `pass` lets it through and counts it; `withhold` replaces it with a notice. Best effort: output the agent itself lets through (its own hook timeout) reaches the model regardless. Default `pass`.
- `tweak_scope` (String) FPE tweak scope: `conversation` / `request` / `tenant`. Defaults to `conversation`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `created_by` (String)
- `endpoint_effect_mapping` (Map of Map of String) Read-only. Per endpoint scope this policy opts into, the authored effects a device enforces differently (authored → applied), e.g. `{ tool_input = { tokenize = "redact" } }`. The format-preserving key never reaches a device, so `tokenize` is always mapped. Empty when no endpoint scope is set.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `policy_id` (String)
- `profile_count` (Number)
- `updated_at` (String)
- `updated_by` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--criteria"></a>
### Nested Schema for `criteria`

Required:

- `conditions` (Attributes List) Conditions evaluated under the parent `operator`. At least one is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--criteria--conditions))
- `operator` (String) Logical operator joining the conditions: `AND` or `OR`.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Optional human-readable description.
- `type` (String) Criteria type. Allowed: `claims`, `context`, `request`, `time`. Server default applies if unset.

<a id="nestedatt--criteria--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `criteria.conditions`

Required:

- `field` (String) Field path to evaluate (e.g. `client_id`, `department`, `email`).
- `operator` (String) Comparison operator (`equals`, `in`, `lt`, `gt`, `ends_with`, …).

Optional:

- `case_sensitive` (Boolean) For string operations. Platform defaults to `true` when omitted.
- `description` (String) Optional description.
- `value` (String) JSON-encoded value to compare against. Examples: `jsonencode("legal")`, `jsonencode(["a","b"])`, `jsonencode(100)`.
- `value_type` (String) Optional type hint for the value (`string`, `int`, `list`, …). The platform defaults it to `string` when unset.
